speaker: Orion
text: The ceiling used to be blue. I painted it myself. How long have those roots been here?

speaker: Innkeeper Bran
text: Bunks are dry, chicory's burnt. You checking in before the night shift whistles?

speaker: Player
text: Just passing through.

speaker: Innkeeper Bran
text: Keep your collar zipped then. Sulfur winds scour the lower mezzanine after curfew.

speaker: Caretaker Iva
text: Mind the yellow chalk marks on the deck—drill crews run knuckle-dice between shifts.

speaker: Player
text: What’s the prize?

speaker: Caretaker Iva
text: Clean air filters and bragging rights. Best currency in the residential shaft.

speaker: Juno
text: Waybill expediter on a tight clock—talk fast or walk the gantry with me.

speaker: Player
text: Any news?

speaker: Juno
text: Ore manifests are coming up short at the cargo hoist. Boggs is sweating an audit. Keep your eyes peeled.

speaker: Sergeant Leto
text: Work permits and clearance chits. Ha—kidding. Dominion forgot our sector's stamps weeks ago.

speaker: Player
text: Anything we should avoid?

speaker: Sergeant Leto
text: Sub-level drainage conduits after shift change. Unless you enjoy wrestling rogue pressure haulers.

speaker: Pasha
text: Step up to the stall! Today's salvage lots are certified genuine and only mildly irradiated!

speaker: Player
text: We're just looking.

speaker: Pasha
text: Looking costs zero credits. But take advice: bid before the patrol drones cycle—night scrap runs fast.

speaker: Rana
text: Watch your boots. Half these freight pallets are rotting under mineral slurry.

speaker: Player
text: Busy day?

speaker: Rana
text: Always. If a container's tagged in blue stencil, it goes to the deep blast zone. Don’t touch blue.

speaker: Sedge
text: You look like someone who knows how to keep quiet around security cameras.

speaker: Player
text: Depends on the secret.

speaker: Sedge
text: Then it depends on your scrip. Come back when you've got salvage worth trading.

speaker: Doctor Sera
text: If you're coughing dust, take a seat. If you're not, don't track grit onto my clean field.

speaker: Player
text: We’re fine.

speaker: Doctor Sera
text: Good. I'm rationing lung balm and sterile dressings as it is.

speaker: Sima
text: Broth is boiling, peppers came off the thermal pipes. Want steam or fire?

speaker: Player
text: Surprise me.

speaker: Sima
text: Bold. I like bold in a miner. Here—blow on it before it blisters your tongue.

speaker: Tallo
text: Fresh off the surface lift? Welcome to the bottom. Bulkheads leak, spirits don’t.

speaker: Player
text: Nice place.

speaker: Tallo
text: It's home. The trick is keeping Dominion from grinding it to dust.

speaker: Ellie
text: Just swapping out panels before the sparks get ambitious. What do you need?

speaker: Ellie
text: The arcade's alive again! Here, a little something for keeping the lights bright.

speaker: Jed
text: There you are. Warden's closing the lift. I've got the bypass held, but the motor's fighting me.

speaker: Nova
text: Zeke's opened a route to the pods. Give me your arm. We're all going.

speaker: Jed
text: Let go of this lever and the brake drops. You'd never reach the other side. I've tried the wrench already, Nova.

speaker: Nova
text: Then we find something else. You always have a spare. Tell me where it is.

speaker: Jed
text: Look at me. Take the Chime. Zeke can use it at the pod.

speaker: Jed
text: I kept fixing your cutter so you'd come home with it. This time, get somewhere they can't send you back.

speaker: Jed
text: Go, Nova. Let me do this much.

speaker: Jed
text: You look like you slept inside the ventilation shaft. Sit. I've saved you the chair that doesn't bite.

speaker: Nova
text: The conduit outside my bunk was live. Ticket says you fixed it yesterday.

speaker: Jed
text: Ticket says somebody fixed it. My name makes the report look reassuring. Let me see your cutter.

speaker: Nova
text: If you take it apart, I'm late for shift. Late means another quota penalty.

speaker: Jed
text: That cold loop splits on shift, you’ll lose fingers. Eat. Bring the parts to my workshop and we’ll fit them.

speaker: Jed
text: Mind the scrap loader in the yard. Its sensor's gone bad. Give it room to turn.

speaker: Jed
text: [Jed taps the bench twice with his wrench. Nova cuts the power; he passes her the lamp.]

speaker: Nova
text: You had a spare waiting. How long have you known this thing was going to fail?

speaker: Jed
text: Since you started calling that noise 'normal.' Kept the spare for you. Next time, bring it in before it whistles.

speaker: Jed
text: Cold loop holds. Now ground the liner to the floor bus. And leave that governor where it belongs.

speaker: Nova
text: Factory sweep leaves twelve percent of the seam behind. They still charge it against my quota.

speaker: Jed
text: I've seen what that extra twelve percent does to a hand. I can mend the cutter, Nova. You make the other job harder.

speaker: Nova
text: One sweep. Liner grounded, cold loop at sixty-eight. If it runs hot, I stop. You can say you told me so all the way home.

speaker: Jed
text: I'd rather have you there to argue with. Patch the liner first. If you're bypassing the governor, confirm it yourself. I won't make that choice for you.

speaker: Jed
text: The breaker logged that surge against your operator ID. I tried to put it under workshop maintenance. They wouldn't take my name.

speaker: Nova
text: Then they pull my shift clearance. The quota doesn't stop because the cutter broke.

speaker: Jed
text: Try Hank at Transit Checkpoint on the hub map. If he turns you away, head east from the Search Bay to Zeke's Booth. He can buy you time. I’ll head for the service lift.

speaker: Jed
text: Transit Checkpoint is on the hub map. Past the Shift Queue, turn east from the Search Bay to Zeke's Booth if Hank rejects you.

speaker: Jed
text: Easy. I’ve got the bypass for now. Keep away from the lift motor.

speaker: Jed
text: Grab a seat if you're sticking around. If something starts smoking, hand me the wrench first.

speaker: Jed
text: You made it back in one piece. That surge settle down once you pulled the core?

speaker: Jed
text: I'll open the housing and see where the signal leads. Good work bringing it back.

speaker: Jed
text: Good. Fewer breakdowns means fewer people eating cold rations. Keep at it.

speaker: Jed
text: Core's cooling on my bench. Once the casing stops ticking, I'll put it to work.

speaker: Jed
text: Smell that ozone? That's the core spool. Hand it over before it cooks through your belt.

speaker: Jed
text: Track the pulse. If the deep mine lit up, something under Sector 4 is drawing power.

speaker: Jed
text: That's all of them. Get this gear back before the owners start charging me storage.

speaker: Schoolteacher Kasey
text: Quiet feet, please. The little ones are mapping constellations they have never been allowed to see.

speaker: Schoolteacher Kasey
text: Wonderful! The kids will be back under the stars tonight. Please, take this for your trouble.

speaker: Maddie
text: Beans are roasting, and for once the grinder is not threatening to explode. Did you need something?

speaker: Maddie
text: You fixed it! Oh, thank you! Take these credits - may your next cup be on me.

speaker: Nova
text: Burrower was feeding on it. Nest is quiet now, but whoever rigged the chamber knew what they were doing.

speaker: Guard Hank
text: Badge on the reader. I've had enough arguments for one morning.

speaker: Nova
text: Morning to you too.

speaker: Guard Hank
text: [The scanner chimes flat and red. Hank's hand stops over the reader. He doesn't look up.]

speaker: Nova
text: Hank? It's just a cutter surge flag. What does it say?

speaker: Guard Hank
text: Rejected. Don't make me read the reason out loud. If the Warden's office pulls your file before Zeke touches it, nobody here can stop it. Booth's east of here.

speaker: Guard Hank
text: Badge ready before you reach the scanner.

speaker: Zeke
text: I can't open the file until Hank logs the rejection.

speaker: Zeke
text: Name, ID, clearance—hang on, the printer's eating its own ribbon again... oh, Nova! You're early. Did Hank send you over, or do you need me to 'accidentally' misfile another late slip?

speaker: Nova
text: Hank rejected my badge. I've got ten minutes before they dock my shift. Can you fix it?

speaker: Zeke
text: Probably. Give me a moment. That flag should be yellow. Why is it...

speaker: Zeke
text: Mandatory retirement. Asset liability exceeds projected value. Disposition: recycle. Nova, don't put your badge back in the reader.

speaker: Nova
text: Retirement? Jed's been here twice as long. What are they taking from me?

speaker: Zeke
text: Everything they can reclaim. It's a disposal order. Usually all I see is the badge number.

speaker: Zeke
text: I can redirect the review to Logistics. The cause has to be a grid fault. Help me choose the field. My hands aren't being useful.

options.text: Grid Instability
Operator Error
Unauthorized Modification

speaker: Zeke
text: Operator error names you as the fault. They'll keep the disposal order. Choose the equipment failure.

speaker: Zeke
text: Unauthorized modification means you meant to do it. That gives them another reason. We need the grid to take the blame.

speaker: Zeke
text: Grid Instability. Submitted. Your badge printed; the review buys you time. Take these supplies too. If anyone asks, I followed procedure. Go before I start shaking again.

speaker: Zeke
text: Keep your voice down. This booth records everything—mostly me sighing at jammed printers, but still. Stand by the corner vent; the mic skips there.

speaker: Zeke
text: I'm opening the pod controls. My hands keep slipping. Keep him away from this panel, Nova. I'll get us a way out.

speaker: Zeke
text: Give me a moment. I like to know what a switch does before someone makes me press it.

speaker: Scrapper
text: You opened it? No alarm? No sweep team? Hah. They really did forget the dead.

speaker: Nova
text: They scratched names into the lid.

speaker: Scrapper
text: Names? Keep those. I don't trade in them. Take the grenades, and don't tell anyone which counter they crossed.

speaker: Scrapper
text: Cutter. You want something the company didn't ration? There's an old resistance cache behind the strip. I know where. You look like you can get it open.

speaker: Nova
text: Why not grab it yourself?

speaker: Scrapper
text: I sell risks. I try not to take them. Open the crate clean and bring me proof there's no live alarm. Then we both get something useful.

speaker: Scrapper
text: Keep the grenades dry. Cheap detonators are how you lose fingers and repeat customers.

speaker: Scrapper
text: Keep your voice down.

speaker: Scrapper
text: Buying, selling, or just looking guilty? Keep it quick either way.

speaker: Doc
text: Hear that? Neither do I. First time that corner of the ward has stopped coughing today. What was wrong?

speaker: Nova
text: Fans were running backward. I rerouted them and cleared the blockage. You should get clean air now.

speaker: Doc
text: Reversed fans. Somebody signed off on that. I'll keep the patients breathing; you take these corrosive rounds. Make sure you get back here under your own power.

speaker: Doc
text: Breathe shallow until you're past the ward. The vents are blowing mine exhaust over people who can barely stand.

speaker: Nova
text: You filed for repairs last week. I carried the request myself.

speaker: Doc
text: They returned it with the box for 'acceptable losses' checked. I have names in those beds. Patch the cracked vent and clear the airflow before I need more empty ones.

speaker: Doc
text: The little one by the window finally slept. Leave the door quiet if you're passing through.

speaker: Doc
text: If you're bleeding, sit. If you're not, don't start.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Nova. I moved your temporary badge to the top of the queue. It kept flashing over my shipment totals.

speaker: Nova
text: Zeke said my file got routed to Logistics review.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Sector 4 needs a cutter, and Compliance fines my shift twice as much for an uncertified injury as a certified one. Pass the Security Post drill and I'll clear the lift.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: East through Customer Service to the Security Post. Break the trainer's shield and log your certification.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: The training log is still blank. Hit the Security Post to the east and finish the shield drill.

speaker: Nova
text: And if I don't?

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Then the lift stays locked. When your override expires, this file goes back to Compliance. Finish the drill while it's still on my desk.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Training's logged. Good. Your badge has stopped being the loudest thing on my screen.

speaker: Nova
text: You promised the Deep Elevator. I've done the drill. Don't send me to another desk.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Sector 4’s relays are failing, and Thorne’s office froze the whole shift’s pay. Nobody else is going down there while the Warden’s sweep teams are patrolling the shafts. You need a clean work log before your override expires; I need that junction running.

speaker: Nova
text: You know my disposal review is still active. You're sending me down there because if the mine takes me, you don't have to file the paperwork.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: I'm giving you the only thing that buys you another shift: completed work beside your name. The lift west of the lobby is cleared for Sector 4. Restore the junction and trace the failed relays. Come back with something I can put in the report.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: You. Cutter. Loader's idle, cargo's blocking my schedule, and your certification log is blank.

speaker: Nova
text: Do you need the cargo moved before I can take the drill?

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Take the drill at Security Post. That’s what gets you down the mine. If you want practice first, the loader and cargo rail are at the Loading Dock.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Your shield certification’s logged. Come see me when you’re ready for Sector 4.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Company time ain't charity. Move.

speaker: Miner Bill
text: Bar's quiet if you ignore the vents. I recommend ignoring the vents.

speaker: The Warden
text: Nova Vance. Your disposal order is under review. Return to your assigned sector and you may still receive a favorable decision.

speaker: Nova
text: Jed stayed behind to hold that lift. You sent guards after him. Open the hatch.

speaker: The Warden
text: One departure becomes a hundred. Every worker watching this bay must see the same answer. Step away from the pod.

speaker: Zeke
text: He’s down. Nova, the security panel’s booting again. Help me with the hatch.

speaker: Nova
text: Here. I’ve got the hatch. Where do you need the Chime?

speaker: Zeke
text: Pass me the Chime once you’re in. I’ll seal the hatch behind us.

speaker: Zeke
text: Jed's Chime fits the console. Check your gear, Nova. I can keep the panel open, but we need it before we try the splice.

speaker: Zeke
text: There's a matching port under this cover. I can wire the Chime in. After that... I've never launched anything with people in it.

speaker: Nova
text: Neither have I. Tell me where it goes. We'll do the next bit together.

speaker: Zeke
text: [He takes the Chime gently from her palm.] Jed really stayed at that lever... didn't he?

speaker: Nova
text: He told me to get somewhere they can't send us back. Let's make sure he didn't hold that shutter for nothing.

speaker: Zeke
text: It took the Chime. Power’s holding. I can get us off the rail. After that, I can’t promise where we’ll land.

speaker: Nova
text: You came with me when staying would've been safer. I'm not leaving you wherever we land. Start the launch sequence.

speaker: Zeke
text: Nova? Say something. I can’t see through this visor.

speaker: Nova
text: Here. Your suit seal is split. Keep it clear of the water until I find a patch.

speaker: Zeke
text: Recycler’s running. One thing I can cross off. The pod core… no. We’re walking.

speaker: Zeke
text: I put Jed's Chime on navigation without tracing the pair. That's on me. It's still glowing in the wrecked console—grab it before the water gets in.

speaker: Zeke
text: Check the wrecked navigation console. We can't leave the Chime in the water.

speaker: Zeke
text: The pod medkit has bio-sealant and pressure tape. That will close the tear in my suit before we follow the glow-water.

speaker: Zeke
text: The stream of glow-water seems to flow deeper into the concrete structures. Let's move before the wreck draws company.

speaker: Zeke
text: I’ve plotted the low airlane. The Astra handles like a loaded hopper. Give yourself room on the turns.

speaker: Zeke
text: Beacon’s straight ahead, through that stone gate. Careful. Those vines cut right through my glove.

speaker: Zeke
text: No password field. The pod wants matching safety readings: mural pattern, pressure, sockets, and coolant.

speaker: Zeke
text: Pressure’s falling. All three rings are holding. I think you can open it now.

speaker: Zeke
text: The rings won’t hold. Check the coolant gauge and the pressure bypass again.

speaker: Zeke
text: That is all five. Ferns, weeds, moss, spores, roots—each handles the same signal differently. We have a map of what this place is doing now. Nice work, Nova.

speaker: Zeke
text: Every plant near the wreck bends toward the Chime. If we are carrying a dinner bell, I would like to know who can hear it. Scan five different specimens for me?

options.text: Sure, I'll scan them.
Not right now.

speaker: Zeke
text: He asked who was supposed to wake him. I pulled up the roster. Every name had the same word beside it. I couldn’t say it out loud.

speaker: Zeke
text: He waited for the ground lead, then offered me his hand. I still kept the wrench where I could reach it. He saw. He held his hand out anyway.

speaker: Orion
text: Four feeds hold the barrier: horn vibration, an ungrounded cup, root pressure, and live breakers. Fix those first.

speaker: Orion
text: There. The system can breathe again, and the barrier has nothing left to hold.

speaker: Orion
text: The barrier hums louder, pushing us back. One of its bands is still being forced out of tune.

speaker: Orion
text: Listen for what each voice does. One supports the others, one answers, and one holds above them. The sockets carry those same roles.

speaker: Orion
text: There. I used to hear them from the courtyard. Let it play a little longer, please.

speaker: Orion
text: Find the crystals in the west, east, and north wings first. I will stay near the mural. I would rather hear all three return together.

speaker: Orion
text: Your hands are shaking again. The shore herbs bind Source residue into resin; we used it after long crossings. Bring clean herbs and meat from Tide Pools. You need food as well as a stabilizer.

options.text: Let's go.
Maybe later.

speaker: Orion
text: The mural has gone quiet. Three crystals were carried into the Sanctuary wings. I knew the people whose voices they hold. Will you help me bring them back?

options.text: I can help with that.
Not right now.

speaker: Orion
text: There should be a path to the shore beneath these roots. I walked it every morning. Give me a moment; I am trying to recognize something.

speaker: Orion
text: Gh0st waited for an order that never came. Then he offered his hand anyway. I trust that choice more than a clean signal.

speaker: Orion
text: I remember the approach from the coast. Keep below the Shield and I can talk you through the turn toward the Spire.

speaker: Orion
text: Give me a moment. I’m listening for what changed when we came in.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Stop there. Hands away from the Chime. My command channel marks you for disposal.

speaker: Nova
text: We got out of the colony alive. Look at me. Is anyone still on that channel?

speaker: Gh0st
text: No confirmation. No reply. I have never had to decide what follows silence.

speaker: Gh0st
text: There is a transmitter beyond the vent security grid. I want its timing crystal, not its command feed. Mask the scans, get past the guards, take the core. I can make it useful.

options.text: I'll fetch it.
Maybe later.

speaker: Gh0st
text: I keep checking the channel. Nothing. You would think silence was easy to get used to.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Airlocks are sealed. I’ll watch the cargo ramp. Go get some sleep.

speaker: Gh0st
text: I’m listening. Go ahead.

speaker: Jax
text: Easy. You're dripping sewer water on my floor, and you've checked the door three times. I'm Jax. This is The Static; people come here to get out of the patrols' way. What happened?

speaker: Zeke
text: Jax found us a roof, and the terminal works. Same Dominion service menus we had back home in the mines. I can ground the wiring, but I can't hide us from the scans.

speaker: Nova
text: Then we make this room safe. Zeke, check the ground. Orion, can you shield us from the scans before we start planning?

speaker: Orion
text: There. I’ve cut the signal at the stairwell. Zeke, check your meter. Can you still pick us up?

speaker: Jax
text: Thorne closed the public lifts when the sweeps started. Her freight still goes up. We can use that.

speaker: Jax
text: Here. Patrol schedules. Get the underrail timing, badges, and uniforms together before you commit at the planning table.

speaker: Jax
text: The sign’s core is burnt out. An Upper City Sentinel carries the same power core; look in the private booths beyond the Exec Lounge when your route takes you upstairs. Bring one back and we can keep the bar looking open.

options.text: I'll get a core for you.
Maybe later.

speaker: Jax
text: You got the core. Install it on the sign console over there.

options.text: Install neon core.

speaker: Jax
text: Still need that sign core. Check the Upper City Sentinels in the private booths beyond the Exec Lounge when your route takes you upstairs.

speaker: Jax
text: The sign’s holding steady and the patrols walked right past the front glass. Keep the stairs clear and the bar stays open.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Nova. That deleted transfer we pulled at the security kiosk—Elara’s case number still links back to Upper City sorting records. If I log into Transit Plaza databases myself, alarms trigger. Help me trace where they moved her.

options.text: I'll search the records.
Not now.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Wait. Stop the scroll. That deleted transfer at the bottom of the staff routes... “Elara.” That’s my sister.

speaker: Nova
text: Your sister? You never mentioned you had family in the Spire.

speaker: Gh0st
text: The compliance chip stripped almost everything before my unit number. Seeing her name... I remember her handwriting, and I remember they took her first. I’m copying the case number. Help me trace it when we have an opening.

speaker: Mika
text: Try the skewers! Real protein today. Also... can you fix these lanterns? When lights fail, patrols call us a hazard and clear the stalls.

options.text: I'll help you fix them.
I'm busy.

speaker: Mika
text: Power’s coming through again. Help me switch it back to the lanterns before another stall packs up.

options.text: Fix lanterns.

speaker: System
text: Ready to move? Wear the copied uniforms to Transit Plaza and use the freight badges at the service lift. It opens at the Upper City laundry intake. Zeke will send the Astra’s autopilot to the rooftop pad. Cover story: scheduled Skypark air-filter inspection.

options.text: Commit the plan and take the service elevator upstairs.
Keep preparing. Leave the table for now.

speaker: Museum Curator
text: Fascinating refraction. Sector 9 lineage? No, not lineage. Salvage.

speaker: Museum Curator
text: [The Curator looks past Orion to Nova.] Keep him beside you. Security will remove anyone without a registry entry.

speaker: Zeke
text: [Zeke lowers his voice as the registry clears.] We’re through. Nova, there’s a loose thread on your cuff. Tuck it in before he looks back.

speaker: Zeke
text: Same scanner grid as the mine. Here’s the maintenance login—they left it taped inside the laundry cabinet. Billions in Upper City security, beaten by a sticky note.

speaker: Zeke
text: There. Scanners are off. The maintenance log says they passed inspection.

speaker: Orion
text: The Prism Gallery forces pressure into light. Read the containment field, shutters, and tether routing before touching the Lens.

speaker: Orion
text: Listen when the shutters close. The hum will drop out for six seconds. That’s when you reach for it.

speaker: Zeke
text: Wait. Energy density is spiking before you touch it. It's reading you back, Nova. Grab it, and the feedback lights us up.

speaker: Thorne
text: [The freight route on the vault display turns red.] Administrator, suspend freight access. Recover the Lens intact. We’ve sold ten years of Harmony access. Every hour this vault is closed, someone asks for their money back.

speaker: Nova
text: Zeke, watch the readout. If it spikes again, tell me before it hits the glass.

speaker: Thorne
text: You’ve taken the Lens. I’ve opened an audit and given Vale recovery access. Administrator, contain the crew. I want the Lens back intact.

speaker: Thorne
text: [Thorne’s countermand flashes DENIED.] He’s taken the guns. Get the Lens off his roof. The launch route still answers to me.

speaker: Vale
text: Recovery access accepted. Seal the roof. Authorize lethal force. Route every voice on the Lens through my channel. Leave it that way when the vault reopens.

speaker: Concierge
text: Welcome to the altitude where price is proof of citizenship.

speaker: Zeke
text: Jax gave us a roof; Orion made it quiet. Now I need enough service records to turn this terminal into a way upstairs.

speaker: Zeke
text: The service-elevator timing is tight down to four seconds. If we miss the freight switch, we're climbing laundry chutes under spotlight.

speaker: Zeke
text: The scanner’s still dark. I keep wanting to check it again. Tell me when it’s time to move.

speaker: Zeke
text: Thorne wasn't kidding. The entire Spire grid is howling. We need to reach the landing pad and get the Astra flying.

speaker: Orion
text: I can hear our footsteps again. If the room starts ringing, tell me before you open the door.

speaker: Orion
text: I’ll listen for the freight switch. When it goes quiet, we move.

speaker: Orion
text: The light in the Archive keeps returning to the same pane. Someone’s holding it there. I’d like to know what happens when they let it go.

speaker: Orion
text: Turn the Lens a little. There. The pull is strongest toward the Foundry.

speaker: Gh0st
text: I checked the stairwell. If you hear boots, stay away from the door. I’ll take it.

speaker: Gh0st
text: I’ll go first at the service elevator. Wait for me to wave you through.

speaker: Gh0st
text: The Curator spoke of Sector 9 as salvage. They categorized Elara the same way before transferring her file.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Thorne signaled Vale directly. Compliance units are mobilizing from the Upper Ring. We cannot be here when they land.

speaker: Hacked Lab Terminal
text: Recorded drone targets loaded. Apply the corrected calibration profile; the terminal will log the operator signature.

speaker: Gh0st
text: I know where the vents are. I crawled through them when I was small.

speaker: Zeke
text: These vents are running hot enough to cook a tank. Give me thirty seconds and a reason to hate this place more.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Project Phantom. That name is on the inside of my skull.

speaker: Nova
text: We can read it together.

speaker: Gh0st
text: My Source Lock caught on your Fork scar. It interrupted the trigger. I waited for the next order. There wasn’t one.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Take this. If I lock up, it buys me time. Wait for me to tell you when I’m ready—and help me bring her down from that Ring.

speaker: Vale
text: Sector 7 is under audit. Unregistered craft detected. No departures until the anomaly is resolved.

speaker: Gh0st
text: These belts carried bodies before they carried machines. Watch the timing.

speaker: Gh0st
text: They made more of me. Faster. Emptier. Put them down before the line teaches them pain.

speaker: Orion
text: Belts cycle, crushers cycle, then a three-second stop. Find the timing relay.

speaker: Nova
text: My scar's burning. Stand back. I think I can hold it.

speaker: Gh0st
text: [A lattice of light snaps into shape above the Anvil, then buckles. Nova slips toward the slag. Gh0st catches her arm.] Let it fall. I've got you.

speaker: Rylos
text: You crossed my factory and left the Anvil in its cradle. All that effort, and Dominion still keeps its prize.

speaker: Gh0st
text: The relic is still in the Forge. We need to take it before we make our move here.

speaker: Rylos
text: Unit 734. Thorne paid for every circuit in this Foundry, including yours. Put down the weapon. I can still log this as a maintenance fault.

speaker: Vale
text: Commander Rylos, bring up the ownership register. Director Thorne’s signature is no longer valid.

speaker: Zeke
text: My seal’s curling at the edge. Check yours before we go past the slag.

speaker: Zeke
text: There’s a production number for every bed in that file. If the line’s still running, show me where they cut its power.

speaker: Zeke
text: Matrix overloaded. No more phantom units crawling off the belts. Now let's crack the Forge and take their Anvil.

speaker: Zeke
text: Rylos is powering up the Titan Walker on the dock. If we don't grab that Deep-Core Engine now, we melt with the facility.

speaker: Orion
text: That pressure wave’s coming through the rail. Take your hand off it a moment. Can you still feel it?

speaker: Orion
text: Gh0st went quiet when the terminal read out his number. Give him a minute before we ask what he remembers.

speaker: Orion
text: The floor’s stopped vibrating. The Anvil’s still beating through the Forge wall. I can follow that.

speaker: Orion
text: The shape held for a breath. We can work on the next breath when we’re clear of the dock.

speaker: Gh0st
text: The airlock pressure cycled. I remember these maintenance pipes. Every vent leads to an intake or an incinerator.

speaker: Gh0st
text: I kept that page. I want to show Elara her correction is still there.

speaker: Gh0st
text: I counted the empty tanks twice. I needed to see the line stop.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Rylos brought the Titan Walker to the dock. He wants to execute us where he built me. Let him try.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Vale kept Thorne’s cipher. I know where she used to put the override. Give me ten seconds.

speaker: Maintenance Bot
text: SOLAR ARRAY OCCLUDED. HORTICULTURAL LOSSES EXCEED EXECUTIVE PRESENTATION LIMITS.

speaker: Maintenance Bot
text: SOLAR ARRAY ALIGNED. HORTICULTURAL CANOPY WITHIN NOMINAL LIGHT PARAMETERS.

speaker: Thorne
text: I sold Harmony by the seat. The Foundry supplied the hardware, and I signed the orders that kept the seats filled. Vale copied my command cipher while your Lens was still warm. Now I can’t open my own doors.

speaker: Vale
text: Welcome to the Ring. Director Thorne is unavailable. Orbital Compliance is acting command. For your safety, remain where you are.

speaker: Thorne
text: The coolant pulse still tells you which branch is live. Follow it through Alpha, Beta, and Gamma. Vale changed the locks while I was inside.

speaker: Thorne
text: The coolant branches lead straight to the Anchor Chamber. Get the Anchor out before Vale finishes routing the Ring through the Throne Room.

speaker: Elara
text: 734. You’re late. I can hold the firewall long enough to open the cradle. Take the Anchor, brother.

speaker: Elara
text: The cradle lock is open. Lift the Anchor out before the Hunter-Killer reaches the tank.

speaker: Elara
text: Follow the cable east to the Throne Room. I can hold the door open from inside the tank.

speaker: Vale
text: [A worker’s voice crackles through the dais. “My sister is still down there.” The voice breaks on the last word. Vale steadies it until it holds a single note.] Do you hear how quiet it can be?

speaker: Zeke
text: That carpet’s trying to float away. Test the next plate before you put your weight on it.

speaker: Zeke
text: Her panel kept taking the code and sending it straight back. She must’ve tried it a hundred times.

speaker: Zeke
text: That coolant gauge has dropped all the way to zero. Keep moving before someone brings the firewall back up.

speaker: Zeke
text: They put Elara on the same diagram as the coolant pumps. No name. Just a port number. I keep looking at it.

speaker: Orion
text: At the dock the floor dropped away for a moment. Keep one hand near the rail. It might happen again.

speaker: Orion
text: There were names on Thorne’s list. I wonder whether Vale ever read them aloud.

speaker: Orion
text: I thought the pulse was coming from the server. It’s still there with the core down. Elara’s ahead.

speaker: Orion
text: I could still hear Elara when we took the Anchor. Let’s get back to her as soon as we can.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Recognized Thorne's security handshake at the dock. Same protocols she used when she tagged me Unit 734.

speaker: Gh0st
text: I used to rehearse what I’d say if I got Thorne alone. Then I saw the lock on her door. All I wanted was the list of names.

speaker: Gh0st
text: That’s Elara’s cipher. Three quick pings, then a gap. She’s still working the lock from her side.

speaker: Gh0st
text: The glass was cold against my hands. She’s still in there, holding the door for us. We need to reach the other end of that cable.

speaker: Zeke
text: I could hear you outside the glass. Kept thinking I’d missed my chance to get up. [Zeke takes a breath.] Can we sit a minute?

speaker: Gh0st
text: I couldn’t save her. The order kept coming anyway. [Gh0st lowers his hands.] I can let it go quiet now.

speaker: Orion
text: I can still hear them in the current. I thought if I waited long enough, someone would come back for me. You did.

speaker: Vale
text: Thorne charged for every voice she let into Harmony. I can reach every room in the Colony at once. No parent will have to tell a child why someone isn’t coming home.

speaker: Nova
text: I wanted to open that door. Then I heard Orion behind me, and Gh0st asking about the people behind the glass. Open the corridor, Vale. Let them decide where they go.

speaker: Zeke
text: My hands are still shaking. Give me a minute by the fire, then I’ll check on the others.

speaker: Zeke
text: The old clock was running slow again. I almost put it right before I remembered whose version of the mine we were in.

speaker: Zeke
text: I thought the plank would drop when I took my foot off it. Look. It’s still there.

speaker: Zeke
text: I’ve got the lead clipped on. If it comes loose up there, call my name. I’ll hear you.

speaker: Orion
text: I spent so long waiting to hear footsteps on that shore. Would you walk with me a little farther?

speaker: Orion
text: You stopped at the lift before you went in. Was that where you used to wait for Jed?

speaker: Orion
text: I could hear the shore behind us. For a second I wanted to go back. Then I heard you up ahead.

speaker: Orion
text: It’s quiet ahead. Keep talking when we go through. It’ll help me find you.

speaker: Gh0st
text: The order stopped. I stayed anyway. I wanted to be here when the rest of you got back.

speaker: Gh0st
text: That lift looked new. I watched you check the bypass before you stepped on. Did Jed teach you that?

speaker: Gh0st
text: I heard Elara on the bridge. Just once. She said my name.

speaker: Gh0st
text: If you lose sight of me, call once. I’ll be close.

speaker: Sentinel-3
text: Trading interface established. Select components for exchange.

speaker: Sentinel-3
text: Core status: 89% coherence. Atmospheric humidity: high. The canopy resonance is vibrating at key G minor today.

speaker: Zeke
text: Patrol beacons scatter their signatures across the Wilds. Triangulate all three before trusting the final vector. Their cutter team may have carried something useful.

speaker: Orion
text: Eat. Hydrate. Take the stabilizer. Your tremor is worse, and the next channel will not care why.

speaker: Orion
text: Those razor-vines carry toxic spores. A heated blade could cauterize them. The patrol transceiver may lead us to a repairable cutter.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Hold position. Blind the gantry grid before you step onto the grate. Guard sweeps cycle fast.

speaker: Orlo
text: Keep your boots dry, kid. The lower drift is humming deeper every cycle.

speaker: Rourke
text: Eat while it’s hot. Found dried herbs in the hopper? Throw them in the cooker with a dry ration. It almost tastes like soup.

speaker: Mira
text: You went into Side Shunt 4? That datapad... those were my shift mates. Dominion sealed the bulkhead and marked them as 'equipment loss.' Keep that Recoil Dampener bolted tight, Nova. Don't let them bury you down here too.

speaker: Mira
text: Watch your fingers near the loader tracks. Dominion doesn’t issue spare knuckles. Jed’s inside. If you get the deep junction running, check Side Shunt 4 for me.

speaker: Scout Kaelen
text: Step into the firelight. Let me see your hands. Did you come down through the canopy?

options.text: I'm Nova. We crashed recently in an escape pod.
Any advice for surviving this coast?
Do you know what's blocking the sky?

speaker: Scout Kaelen
text: Another crash? Six months ago my reconnaissance cutter hit that violet sky barrier. The hull broke apart. The people at the falls helped me survive. I watch the beach now and trade what I find, but my patrol never came back from inland.

speaker: Scout Kaelen
text: Use heat on razor-vines. A cold blade bursts the spore pods. If you hear a low hum in the mist, get off the ridge. The Beast hunts by sound.

speaker: Scout Kaelen
text: The old records call it the Curfew Shield. My hull folded the moment I crossed it. You can still fly below it. If you want off the planet, start with the people who built that temple.

speaker: Scout Kaelen
text: Take this ration pack and antidote flask. You'll need every scrap of padding if you're pushing into the canopy.

speaker: Scout Kaelen
text: Use heat on razor-vines. A cold blade bursts the spore pods. If you hear a low hum in the mist, get off the ridge. The Beast hunts by sound.

speaker: Scout Kaelen
text: Keep your boots dry and your blade sharp, Nova. The tide turns fast on this coast.

options.text: How are you holding up out here on your own?
I've gathered fresh herbs and beast meat from the wilds.
I found your scout patrol's beacon in the Burned Glade. I recovered their Thermal Cutter.
Remind me about the coastal hazards.

speaker: Caretaker Echo
text: [Chime chime]... Carrier frequency detected. Resonance signature: Uncalibrated Visitor. Sanctuary archive systems operating at thirty-eight percent capacity.

options.text: What is Sanctuary?
Who is asleep in the Stasis Chamber?
We opened the pod. What were its safeguards for?
We woke Orion. What do the records say about him?
How do we breach the Curfew Shield?

speaker: Caretaker Echo
text: Sanctuary is a Class-4 Harmonic Vault. When the Great Severance contaminated outer frequencies, this facility was sealed to preserve the Core Navigator lineages until the stars stabilized.

speaker: Caretaker Echo
text: Navigator Caste, First Division. The stasis shell keeps the sleeper's memory bands separate while pressure passes around them. Forcing the pod without calibration risks neural shear.

speaker: Caretaker Echo
text: The Source Gate protects the hangar approach. Ground its emitters and restore power to the Astra before releasing the launch cradle. These are local departure procedures; they do not provide passage through the outer Planetary Shield.

speaker: Caretaker Echo
text: Archive buffers stand ready. Continue harmonic alignment, traveler.

speaker: Scout Kaelen
text: David shares what he can, but the camp's stores are thin. My knee still won't stand a hunt through the thickets. Bring two herbs and one cut of beast meat for the pot, and I'll fit your weapon with my division's precision sight.

speaker: Scout Kaelen
text: Let's see what you brought.

speaker: Scout Kaelen
text: [Kaelen turns the cutter over and rubs a nick in the handle.] Leto. I filed three requests to go back for him. Never got past the glade. Keep the cutter, Nova. Here’s a battery that’ll fit.

speaker: Rylan
text: Keep clear of the runoff valve unless you want your soles fused to the grating. If you brought scrap from the upper levels or need thermal plating, speak up.

options.text: Need any help around the welder bench?
I brought the heavy gear and hydraulic fluid you needed.
I found Talia's worker tablet near the cooling pool.
What can you tell me about the heat deeper in the Foundry?
I should get going.

speaker: Rylan
text: The crushers took out my press manifold. Bring me one Heavy Gear and one Hydraulic Fluid. Once the ram’s moving, I can fit you a Heat Liner.

speaker: Rylan
text: [Rylan works the press. It holds pressure without a hiss.] There. Try that liner on before you head back to the Forge.

speaker: Rylan
text: [Rylan wipes the tablet on his sleeve.] Talia marked the safe route. She must’ve stayed to vent it. Leave the tablet with me, would you? Take a plate from my rack.

speaker: Rylan
text: Past the conveyors is the Anvil. They keep the tether running through cooling breaks now. Watch the vents before you cross.

speaker: Cheno
text: Hey there, Nova! Watch your step around those cable drums—high-tension steel doesn't forgive careless boots. What can I do for you? If your ship's in a bind or you need something hauled, you came to the right deck.

options.text: What is the rigging crew working on up here?
Do you help with the sound for The Static?
You seem to know everyone on this deck.
Who's that in the photo on your tool locker?
Need an extra pair of hands on the rigging?
I brought the heavy gears and wiring bundles for the center truss.
I'll see you around. Take care.

speaker: Cheno
text: We shore up the transit arches and run power to the lower wards. See that cable? If I don’t have it tensioned by shift change, the trains wait.

speaker: Cheno
text: Every weekend, kid. I used to haul amps with Chris and Andrew. If you can make a kick drum carry through a packed cargo hold, you can wire a monitor in your sleep.

speaker: Cheno
text: I’ve had to call for a tow at three in the morning. You remember who picks up. Around here, I try to pick up.

speaker: Cheno
text: The storm tore out two load dampers. I need two Heavy Gears and two Wiring Bundles before the first train. Bring them up and I’ll press you a carabiner from my own stock.

speaker: Cheno
text: [Cheno clamps the new dampers in place and watches the truss settle.] Good. We can run trains tonight. Here’s your carabiner. I filed the burr off the gate for you.

speaker: Chris
text: Watch your step over those patch cables. Dominion pipes four synthetic chords into every elevator to keep productivity up and blood pressure down. We broadcast the other eight. What brings you to our corner of the grid?

options.text: I saw your Wayfarer tour poster taped to the window.
I was just talking with Cheno out on the rigging deck.
Are you two working on a new broadcast?
I brought the rapid capacitor and wiring bundle for your broadcast rig.
What are the lyrics you're working on?
I'll see you around. Take care.

speaker: Chris
text: We screen-printed it in a damp basement. Played cargo holds, bars, one gravel lot where the generator quit halfway through the set. I think that was the best one.

speaker: Chris
text: He once hauled our amps through sleet, mixed the whole show, then asked if we could stop for pizza. Three in the morning. Of course we stopped.

speaker: Chris
text: It’s about leaving a place and calling it home for years afterward. I’ve got the first verse. The second still sounds like a letter I should just send.

speaker: Chris
text: Our transit-tunnel pirate transmitter blew a capacitor during the last security sweep. Bring me 1 rapid capacitor and 1 wiring bundle, and Andrew and I can bypass the jammer and light up the airwaves.

speaker: Chris
text: Andrew, solder the bypass. I’ll patch the output. [Andrew strikes a chord. The monitors carry it cleanly.] There it is. Nova, see if you can still hear us when you get back to the stairs.

speaker: Andrew
text: Hey. Good to see friendly eyes in here. Take a breath—the world outside this car moves entirely too fast. We're just restringing the acoustic rig and trying to get these coils to sing.

options.text: What kind of music do you play?
It feels surprisingly peaceful in here.
Do you miss the old days on the road?
Play something for the room.
I'll see you around. Take care.

speaker: Andrew
text: Acoustic lines with space to breathe. In a city full of synthesized sirens and neon glare, people forget how warm wooden resonance feels. We play the kind of chords that make you want to call an old friend.

speaker: Andrew
text: [Andrew sets his guitar on the bench and opens his arms. He waits for Nova to lean in.] You can stay a minute. The next patrol’s still a ways off.

speaker: Andrew
text: I miss hearing Cheno laugh from the back of the van. Chris and I still play the old set sometimes. We always start too fast.

speaker: Andrew
text: [Andrew plays a few bars and lets the last chord ring.] That’s ‘The Long Drive Home.’ We used to play it last.

speaker: Andrew
text: [Andrew wipes the flux off his fingers.] Thanks, Nova. I wasn’t sure anyone wanted to hear us anymore.

speaker: Nova
text: I heard you through the floor before I found the car. I came up to hear the rest. Keep playing.

speaker: Chris
text: [Chris turns the monitor up and hands Nova a worn pick.] First tour. I’ve got a spare. Andrew, from the top?

speaker: David
text: Come in under the falls and warm yourself. I'm David. A few of us keep this camp and the old station going. There's brisket on the smoker, and Penny will make sure nobody gets left out.

options.text: That brisket smells incredible. Where'd you learn to cook like this?
You look right at home out here by the waterfall.
How do you keep this camp supplied so far out on the coast?
Have you been down to the beach cliffs to the east?
Who's this big fluffy dog keeping watch over the camp?
How do you keep this whole camp running so neatly?
Thanks, David. I should get going.

speaker: David
text: Low heat and a lot of waiting. I put another cut on when I hear someone’s overdue. Gives the rest of us an excuse to stay up.

speaker: David
text: When the Dominion closed the shipping settlements, some of us stayed along the coast. The falls give us shelter, and we know the paths between here and Tidewatch. I always liked camping. Didn't expect it to become the address.

speaker: David
text: Thirty years in supply taught me to keep a little back and know who needs what. We trade salvage, stretch the provisions, and share the cooking. Megan keeps our water clean at Tidewatch. Kaelen brings news from the beach when his knee allows it.

speaker: David
text: [David looks toward the eastern bluffs with a soft, affectionate smile.] I have. There's a spot right out on the edge where the morning sun warms the stone. Two of the best companions a man could ever ask for used to love running that sand. If you walk out there, give 'em a nod for me.

speaker: Ren
text: Hot broth or crispy noodles? Eat while it's steaming, friend. The rain out here cools soup in seconds.

speaker: Cameron
text: Watch your arms around those bypass elbows—that line's carrying steam at six hundred degrees and twelve atmospheres. I'm Cameron, lead pipe-fitter on this deck. What brings you down to the hot lines?

options.text: How long have you been on this shift? You look exhausted.
Who taught you how to fit high-pressure steam conduits?
Are those racing decals on your welding helmet?
Is that a photo of your family on the toolbox?
Whose collar is that hanging beside the gloves?
Need an extra hand getting this bypass sealed?
I found the composite plates and hydraulic fluid for the manifold.
I should get going.

speaker: Cameron
text: Double yesterday. Three hours on the locker bench. I’ll sleep when that gauge holds long enough for the next shift to take it.

speaker: Cameron
text: My dad, Sherman. He used to make me run a finger over every seam before we clocked out. Those are his gloves. I still reach for them when a weld gives me trouble.

speaker: Cameron
text: [Cameron taps the checkered flag on his helmet.] Twenty-four. I used to listen for the engine coming out of the turn. You listen to a steam elbow the same way. If the note changes, get back.

speaker: Cameron
text: Lily, Emma, and Hannah. Kasey sent that picture after Lily’s game. Emma’s trying to steal the glove and Hannah’s got both hands in the orange slices. I missed that one. I’m trying to get back for the next.

speaker: Cameron
text: The relief bypass blew its seal. I need two Composite Plates for the collar and one Hydraulic Fluid for the actuator. Bring those and I’ll give you a wrench off my rack.

speaker: Cameron
text: [Cameron fits the collar and waits for the gauge to settle.] Twelve atmospheres. No hiss. Here. Dad stamped that wrench before he gave it to me. Keep it where you can reach it.

speaker: Charles
text: Keep your voice down near that gate. [Charles angles his slate away from the customs scanner, leaving the public departure board visible.] I can help you read the station's schedules. Passenger records and access codes stay sealed. What do you need?

options.text: Are you running financial models or playing a game on that slate?
You sound like someone who's spent a lifetime reviewing other people's systems.
What's that 'Great Frontier' folder on your screen?
Why help someone breaking through Dominion customs?
Could your analytics help tune my tactical heuristics?
Here are the boards and lens for the tap.
What do you need me to check at the gate?
I should get going.

speaker: Charles
text: Both. My raid group figured out which seller was holding the upgrade parts. I checked the Ring’s berth records the same way. You’d be surprised how often a queue has an owner.

speaker: Charles
text: I have. I start with the bit they say can’t break. If it holds, I’ll tell them. If it doesn’t, I’d rather find out before they’ve put a year into it.

speaker: Charles
text: A friend’s story set to music. He sent me every track. We spent three nights arguing over two bars of a chorus. He kept one.

speaker: Charles
text: [Charles taps the public departure board.] I ran forecasts for Thorne’s contractors. Staff shuttles sat full while her executives flew out half-empty. Now Vale won’t let those workers leave at all. You can check the delays yourself. Their names stay off my slate.

speaker: Charles
text: Check the wait times on my slate against the public board at the biometric gates. Berths and departures only. Bring two Circuit Boards and a Focusing Lens, too. If the timings hold up, I can build you a slate from the feed.

speaker: Charles
text: The public board is at the biometric gates. Compare its departures with my slate. I’m checking whether someone’s holding the berths. For the tap, I still need two Circuit Boards and one Focusing Lens.

speaker: Charles
text: [Charles seats the boards and watches the times settle.] You caught the priority holds. I missed them. Here’s the Venture Heuristic Slate. It’ll help you place a shot. I’ve left the passenger feed disconnected.

speaker: Charlie
text: [A gray-and-white face peeks from the hollow. You take a step, and Charlie backs away. A spore puff rolls out toward your boot.]

options.text: [Leave a reed treat by the hollow and back away]
[Toss the spore puff ball gently across the mossy glade]
[Kneel down, open your arms, and let him approach at his own pace]
[Scratch Charlie’s head and play fetch]
[Sit on the moss and let Charlie curl up beside you]
[Give Charlie some space and step away]

speaker: Charlie
text: [Charlie sniffs the treat, pulls it into the hollow, and watches you with his chin on his paws.]

speaker: Charlie
text: [Charlie pounces on the puff, tumbles over his paws, then bats it back with a chirp.]

speaker: Charlie
text: [Charlie buries his head in the crook of your arm and purrs. When he pulls away, there’s a smooth, glowing stone in your palm.]

speaker: Charlie
text: [Charlie tears after the puff and skids back with it in his jaws. He nudges your hand to get you to throw again.]

speaker: Charlie
text: [Charlie curls against your boots, nose under his tail. The purr keeps going after he closes his eyes.]

speaker: Jason
text: Watch the guitar leads. I’m checking the clock on this signal bus. Or I was, before I opened the star chart. What did you need?

options.text: What are you making in here? There's gear everywhere.
Is that a simulated galaxy on your terminal?
Do you ever actually finish a project?
You look like you genuinely love what you do.
What's that small copper coil on the corner of your bench?
Who's the hefty charcoal cat glaring at me from the tube amp?
I'll see you around. Take care.

speaker: Jason
text: [Jason looks from the star chart to the open guitar pedal.] Which thing? I’ve got a synth patch, a star map, and a nutrition tracker running. I sat down to fix the guitar. Ask my wife what time that was.

speaker: Jason
text: Six worlds in a little model. I’ve got an old mining colony and a ship called the Astra. The flight path works. I’m still figuring out what the crew says to each other on the long stretches.

speaker: Jason
text: Eventually. Chris, Andrew, Cheno, and Charles have all had a go at this one. Every time I cross a page out, one of them gives me something worth putting back in.

speaker: Jason
text: I had Chris try a build last night. He found a bad turn I’d been staring at for a week. Then he asked to play it again. That’ll keep me at the bench.

speaker: Jason
text: [Jason lifts a copper coil from the bench.] Field tuner. You can have this one. I’m already halfway through winding the next.

speaker: Oliver
text: [Oliver opens one eye from his bunk cushion and gives a single, impatient meow.]

options.text: [Report for shift inspection]
[Remind Oliver that mealtime is in five minutes]
[Offer respectful chin scratches]
[Offer respectful chin scratches]
I'll see you around. Take care.

speaker: Oliver
text: [Oliver sniffs your sleeve, gives one slow blink, and tucks his paws back under his chest.]

speaker: Oliver
text: [Oliver’s ears prick. He stretches, trots toward the mess, and looks back to see if you’re following.]

speaker: Oliver
text: [Oliver leans into your knuckles and starts purring. A brass chronometer tag slides out from under his paw.]

speaker: Oliver
text: [Oliver leans into your knuckles and starts purring.]

speaker: David
text: That’s Penny. She’ll bring you a pine cone, then act offended when you throw it. Leave her a spot by the smoker when she’s done making her rounds.

speaker: Penny
text: [Penny circles the crew, nudging each person with her nose until everyone is standing together.]

options.text: [Wrestle with Penny]
[Offer another playful tussle]
[Scratch Penny behind the ears]
[Let Penny settle back beside the campfire]

speaker: Penny
text: [Penny bats at your arms until she tires herself out and flops onto the warm stone. She pushes her red bandana into your hand.]

speaker: Penny
text: [Penny bats at your arms, rolls onto her back, and waits with all four paws in the air.]

speaker: Penny
text: [Penny leans against your legs. With the crew all in sight, she rests her chin on your boot.]

speaker: Megan
text: I'm Megan. This is Tidewatch—an old monitoring station we use for clean water and a little clinical care. If you've come through the marsh, check your suit seals before you sit down. The spores get into everything.

options.text: How does Tidewatch help the camp?
You keep detailed notes on these samples.
The sticky note on your telemetry monitor mentions calling 'Jason'—who's that?
Have you seen that big fluffy sheepadoodle over at the falls?
Do you need anything to keep the filters running?
I brought the catalyst and filament for the filter.
Thanks, Megan. I should get going.

speaker: Megan
text: The station used to monitor the coast. We patched up its filters so the people at the falls have safe drinking water. My background is clinical hygiene: careful cleaning, spotting trouble early, keeping a small problem from becoming everyone's problem.

speaker: Megan
text: I've always liked working out what the evidence says. A residue on a filter, a damaged seal, the same symptoms in two people—small things can point to a bigger problem. I keep notes, compare samples, and try not to jump to conclusions.

speaker: Megan
text: Jason's my husband. He helped patch this equipment together. He'll follow a wiring fault for hours and forget his tea. I make sure he takes a break occasionally.

speaker: Megan
text: Penny checks on me whenever David lets her out of his sight. She seems convinced we're one badly organized flock. Give her a scratch for me if you're heading back to the falls.

speaker: Megan
text: The camp's water filter is clogging with runoff from inland. I need one Chemical Catalyst to treat the residue and one Nano Filament spool for a replacement filter. Help me keep it running and you can take my spare field bio-scanner.

speaker: Megan
text: [Megan checks the first clear sample.] That’ll keep David’s water safe. Take the scanner. If it says you’re overdoing it, sit down and drink something.

speaker: Evelyn
text: [Evelyn hums as she mists the orchids.] Hello, darling. Mind the roots. Robert and I keep this garden going. The blue ones get Monk before breakfast.

options.text: Do the plants really respond to jazz?
You mentioned family?
Is that gentleman over there trying to climb an invisible ladder?
Your orchids look exceptionally vibrant.
I'll let you get back to it. Take care.

speaker: Evelyn
text: A little Monk and up they come. I can’t prove that, but I’m not about to risk a morning without him. My father played records for me. I did the same for Jason.

speaker: Evelyn
text: Tyson made me a paper orchid. Ian drew a dinosaur eating it. Both are in the garden ledger, if you’d like to see.

speaker: Evelyn
text: That’s Robert, my husband. He used to do mime before he started making industrial mops. Ask him about a buffer and he’ll show you how it turns. Ask where he left the key and you’ll get the whole act.

speaker: Evelyn
text: [Evelyn snips a blue blossom.] Take this one, sweetheart. Blue Horizon. Pin it where you can see it when things get loud.

speaker: Robert
text: [Robert points to a scuff on the glass, clutches his chest, then produces his mop with a flourish.]

options.text: [Smile and mime polishing an invisible pane of glass back at him]
You built a company out of specialized mops?
Evelyn said you were looking for something?
Your industrial equipment is seriously impressive.
I'll let you get back to it. Take care.

speaker: Robert
text: [Robert breaks into a grin.] Splendid wrist work. Keep that up and I’ll put you on the orbital decks. Thirty thousand square meters. We take tea at four.

speaker: Robert
text: Started with a loop that wouldn’t fling water over the rails. Then the shipyards called. These days I’d rather have tea and listen to Evelyn’s records, but I still keep a spare head in the cart.

speaker: Robert
text: [Robert pats his pockets.] The buffer key. I had it on the third tee. Unless I watered the hydrangeas first. Evelyn will know.

speaker: Robert
text: [Robert spins a flywheel on the cart.] Feel that settle? Take it. I’ve got another in the shop, and this one will do more good on your gear.

speaker: Pam
text: Sit and eat before you fall over, Nova. Rourke’s got the kitchen going. What do you need?

options.text: Is that a ceramic rooster on the shelf?
Who’s in those photos behind the till?
You don't mince words, do you?
Got anything warm to take into the deep shafts?
Thanks, Pam. I'll let you get back to it.

speaker: Pam
text: [Pam folds her arms.] Back in the mountains, a rooster meant morning. Down here the shift bell does his job. I kept the rooster anyway.

speaker: Pam
text: Megan’s working at a clinic on the coast. Cameron’s on the hot pipes, same work his father Sherman did. He’d have been proud of both of them. I keep their photos behind the till, next to the grandbabies and Kodi and Bella.

speaker: Pam
text: If you’re being a fool, I’ll tell you. Then I’ll make you a plate. Now sit down.

speaker: Pam
text: [Pam wraps a tin in a towel and presses it into Nova’s hands.] Pepper gravy’s underneath. Eat them before you go down the shaft. Rourke will tell me if you don’t.

speaker: Jason
text: That’s Meeko. I cleared the chair for him and he took the amplifier. Pretty sure he’s waiting for me to offer him the chair again.

speaker: Meeko
text: [Meeko lifts his chin from the warm amplifier and waits to see what you’ll do.]

options.text: [Give Meeko a respectful nod]
[Slow-blink at Meeko]
[Attempt to baby-talk Meeko like a cute little kitty]
[Inquire about Jason's working habits]
[Step back and say goodbye.]

speaker: Meeko
text: [Meeko gives one slow nod and pushes a brass connector across the amp with his paw.]

speaker: Meeko
text: [Meeko blinks once and settles both paws over the edge of the amp.]

speaker: Meeko
text: [Meeko’s tail flicks. He turns his head away.]

speaker: Meeko
text: [Meeko looks from Jason’s soldering iron to the unoccupied chair. One claw taps the amp casing.]

speaker: Cheno
text: That’s Angela on the porch. Raegan’s singing again. Brody was halfway out the door for football practice, but he stuck around until she finished. I keep it there for the long shifts.

speaker: Cameron
text: [Cameron touches the collar.] Smokey. Bella’s brother. Almost thirteen years he slept by the hearth while the girls did their lessons. I still step over that spot when I go home.

speaker: David
text: [David wipes the cutting board.] Nancy keeps the place running. I keep the fire going. If she ever finds grease in the flour tin again, I’ll be keeping the fire going outdoors.

speaker: Dax
text: I swear on my license, I only poured his synth-sparkler! The dispenser logs every milliliter—you can check it yourself at the bar!

speaker: Nova
text: Did anyone else approach the glass?

speaker: Dax
text: I had my back turned prepping garnishes for Director Sorrell. But the terminal records every badge ping in this room!

speaker: Dr. Lyra
text: Before you ask: yes, I handle binary coolants. And no, I didn't kill Malick. He was the one auditing Procurement to clear my record. Why would I poison my only ally?

speaker: Dr. Lyra
text: Malick was going to put his name on the audit so Procurement would have to answer him. I’m filing it under mine. They already demoted me once. I know what it could cost. Dax is keeping a copy in case mine disappears.

speaker: Selene
text: I was up on stage singing 'Spire Falling' under three spotlights from 21:10 to 21:25. If someone poisoned Malick, they did it while everyone was watching me.

speaker: Director Sorrell
text: Do not waste my time, scrapper. I am a tier-four director! I've been seated at this corner table on an encrypted conference call since 21:00 sharp. My comms rig logs prove I never left my seat!

options.text: Let's check your alibi against the records.
Never mind for now.

speaker: Director Sorrell
text: What?! That's... that is an outrageous fabrication! A timestamp glitch in the logging firmware!

speaker: Nova
text: The access record puts you in the booth. Cyano-Coolant 9 is in Malick's glass, and its core is missing from the comms rig bearing your crest. A logging fault doesn't empty a coolant bracket.

speaker: Director Sorrell
text: Malick was filing the scrap-contract audit in the morning. My signature was on the transfers. Forty years climbing the Spire, and one report could end it all.

speaker: Director Sorrell
text: [Sorrell sets his passkey on the table.] I took the coolant from my rig. I put it in his glass. Leave the recorder running. I’ll tell security where to find the contracts.

speaker: Pitmaster Brutus
text: Hail the Crucible Champion! The loaders still buzz about your bout. Wear that Forge-Plate proud out there in the Foundry!

speaker: Pitmaster Brutus
text: The Champion’s down! You cleared all three bouts. Come get your Forge-Plate before the crowd climbs the rail.

speaker: Pitmaster Brutus
text: By the core, you cracked a Slag Golem wide open! The betting pool just went into meltdown! Only one match left: my personal masterwork, the Crucible Champion Juggernaut!

options.text: Bring out your Champion!
Hold on, let us prepare first.

speaker: Pitmaster Brutus
text: Sound the sirens! The Champion enters the ring! Show me what starborn steel is made of!

speaker: Pitmaster Brutus
text: Ha! Turned those buzzing pests into molten scrap! But don't celebrate yet—the floor vents are heating up, and the heavy hitters are waiting behind the blast doors.

options.text: Release Round 2: The Molten Crushers!
We need a minute to patch our armor.

speaker: Pitmaster Brutus
text: Pneumatics releasing! Watch the floor vents—here comes the Slag Golem and its field welder crew!

speaker: Pitmaster Brutus
text: Well, look what crawled out of the slag chutes. A fresh crew with genuine starborn chrome. You looking to bet on the scrap bouts, or did you come to bleed in the Crucible?

options.text: What is the Scrapper's Crucible?
We're ready. Bring on Round 1: Magma Drone Swarm!
Just scoping out the pits.

speaker: Pitmaster Brutus
text: Three bouts. Drones with a welder, then the Slag Golem, then my Champion and its escort. You can pull out and rest between bouts. Win all three and the Forge-Plate’s yours.

options.text: Let's do this. Open the cage for Round 1!
Give us a moment to prepare.

speaker: Pitmaster Brutus
text: Cage gates dropping! Keep your shields up and your footing cool—first wave is the Magma Drone Swarm!

speaker: Rebel Terminal
text: Spoof recovered. Network traffic and account writes are audited. Recover the key without leaving a Dominion record.

speaker: Rebel Terminal
text: The recovered key is ready. Which output should receive it?

options.text: Upload to the maintenance network
Write to the removable circuit board
Install in the local supervisor account
Disconnect for now

speaker: Rebel Terminal
text: The upload would register the rebel key with Dominion monitoring. The terminal blocks the write; the recovered key remains available.

speaker: Rebel Terminal
text: Local accounts still report to Dominion compliance. That would tie the spoof to an identity. The terminal blocks the write; choose an isolated output.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: The drill frame logged your run already. I can attach that result to your certification.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Your drill result is in the frame log. Give me a second to register your certification.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Certification is logged. Now we can discuss your Sector 4 assignment.

speaker: Stasis Console
text: The pod is ready. Set pressure, memory, then return. The mural shows an outer pressure bypass; separate memory bands protect the sleeper.

speaker: Stasis Console
text: Pressure ring: the Source is pushing against the pod. Where should it go?

options.text: Divert pressure around the memory shell.
Force pressure through the memory shell.
Step away.

speaker: Stasis Console
text: The pod isolates memories from pressure. Use the outer bypass; forcing current through the sleeper would hurt him.

speaker: Stasis Console
text: Memory ring: the separate carrier bands are holding. How should they connect?

options.text: Collapse the bands into one stronger signal.
Keep each identity on its own band.
Step away.

speaker: Stasis Console
text: The mural preserves distinct voices. A louder merged signal would erase the separation the pod protects.

speaker: Stasis Console
text: Return ring: the coolant is stable. Complete the waking circuit.

options.text: Reconnect return after the outer bypass settles.
Close the bypass and return everything at once.
Step away.

speaker: Stasis Console
text: Closing the bypass would put pressure back through the sleeper. Keep relief open while return reconnects.

speaker: Orion
text: Twenty years. Everyone on the night watch—the whole First Division... twenty years gone behind three inches of frost while I thought I’d wake to the evening tide.

speaker: Zeke
text: The Dominion scrubbed Sector 9 off the flight charts and sealed the canopy under the Planetary Shield almost two decades ago. Nobody’s walked down here since. What drove you into that pod?

speaker: Orion
text: A containment breach. The Dominion outpost dragged a canopy predator out of the swamp after the dynamo leaks warped it—it hunted anything tuned to Source resonance. When their cage failed, it tore straight through our lower doors. I fired the brass Chime down the conduit to get it away from them... and muted the room so it couldn’t hear me breathing.

speaker: Nova
text: The brass Chime? That’s what led us here from the Mining Colony. Your signal has been calling through the dark for twenty years.

speaker: Orion
text: I can still hear each voice on its own—not blurred together. You kept the bands apart. Thank you, Nova. For answering.

speaker: Source Gate Console
text: The grounded receiver is ready. The gauge reads BLEED, then STARVE. Once pressure falls and the lock loses power, Orion can settle the remaining chord.

speaker: Source Gate Console
text: Route 1: living roots are under pressure. Select the relief path.

options.text: Open the root relief into the grounded receiver.
Feed root pressure back into the horn.
Step away.

speaker: Source Gate Console
text: The horn amplifies pressure. Route relief into the grounded cup so the roots can breathe.

speaker: Source Gate Console
text: Relief is flowing into the receiver. The breaker still feeds the lock. Choose the final switch position.

options.text: Boost the lock supply to overpower the barrier.
Isolate the lock supply; keep the relief path open.
Step away.

speaker: Source Gate Console
text: More power makes the barrier clamp harder. Isolate its feed while preserving root relief.

speaker: Mural Array
text: The west crystal carries the low support voice, east the answering voice, north the high stabilizer. Three sockets show a foundation, paired arcs, and a star.

speaker: Mural Array
text: Foundation socket: which crystal supports the chorus?

options.text: West crystal.
North crystal.
Step away.

speaker: Mural Array
text: The west voice supports the others. The bright north voice belongs to the star socket.

speaker: Mural Array
text: The remaining sockets show paired arcs and a star.

options.text: North in the arcs; east in the star.
East in the arcs; north in the star.
Step away.

speaker: Mural Array
text: East answers in paired arcs. North stabilizes the chorus from the star socket.

speaker: Vent Scanner
text: Two narrow scan pulses are followed by a long maintenance gap. The console can latch a mask to one part of that pattern.

speaker: Vent Scanner
text: Choose the mask timing before crossing the hatch.

options.text: Latch the mask to the long maintenance gap.
Transmit during the two narrow scan pulses.
Step away.

speaker: Vent Scanner
text: The narrow pulses are active scans. Use the long maintenance gap; a wrong choice leaves you at the console without raising an alert.

speaker: Astra Navigation
text: Low service airlane to the Spire plotted beneath the Planetary Shield. Cargo ramp open. Confirm departure from the bridge when the crew is ready.

options.text: Close the ramp, release the cradle and depart.
Stay docked for now.

speaker: Nova
text: We just got here. I’m Nova—that’s Zeke. The stasis clock on your pod says twenty years, four months. Is there someone we should look for?

speaker: Zeke
text: Easy, Orion. Sit a minute and catch your breath. Twenty years is a hell of a long time to wake up to all at once—we can check the records when you’re ready.

speaker: Orion
text: I’ve spent long enough in this room. There’s a Bridge in the sealed cradle. It links willing carriers, one voice to a band, but it needs a ground. I’ll show you. Then we should see who’s been watching us from the ridge.

speaker: Zeke
text: Nova? It's Zeke. I found a maintenance route. Follow the red strobes to the cargo lift. I'm keeping it open.

speaker: Zeke
text: Lift gate's open. Please tell me you're on this side of it. Jed's headed for the manual bypass; he's going to hold it while I bring the car across.

speaker: Zeke
text: The car’s here. Watch the gap. Jed’s holding the bypass for us.

speaker: Orion
text: Orion. My name is Orion. Twenty years... no, the calibration must be drifting. I only sealed the hatch after the far bulkhead gave way.

speaker: Nova
text: Keep the rifle down while you work it out. We want to get out of here alive.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Wait. Something is moving behind you. Get clear of the roots.

speaker: Orion
text: That low hum—it’s the same creature that broke through the Sanctuary doors twenty years ago! It tracked the Chime straight up the ridge. Stand your ground!

speaker: Caretaker Echo
text: The shell preserves separate memory bands. The outer bypass carries pressure around the sleeper; it must remain open during waking. This archive records the safeguards, not the occupant's present condition.

speaker: Caretaker Echo
text: Orion. Navigator Caste, First Division. The archived calibration assigns him a distinct carrier band. That separation protects his memories; preserving it matters beyond the pod. My records cannot tell you what he remembers now.

speaker: Mika
text: The cable runs over Lantern Bridge toward an executive billboard. Follow the power siphon before touching the lantern coupling.

speaker: Hacked Lab Terminal
text: Target profile not reviewed. Inspect the prototype targeting audit at Drone Test Alcove before calibrating the rack.

speaker: Director Sorrell
text: I've been at my corner table on an encrypted call since 21:00. My comms logs will confirm it. Ask someone whose time you can afford.

speaker: Director Sorrell
text: [Under guard, Sorrell keeps his eyes on the floor. His credentials have been seized and the confession is on file.] I have nothing further to say.

speaker: Prism Controls
text: The Lens is still under pressure. Choose where to send the relief flow.

options.text: Open the relief socket into blue RETURN.
Send relief back into red FEED.
Vent pressure into gold AUTHORIZATION.
Leave the controls.

speaker: Prism Controls
text: The return now carries pressure away from the Lens. Which shutter should be closed?

options.text: Close blue RETURN.
Close red FEED; keep blue RETURN open.
Release the handles and step away.

speaker: Prism Controls
text: Pressure is relieved and the feed is isolated. The gold tether still reports containment to the Administrator.

options.text: Cut the gold tether.
Copy the local hold signal, then disconnect the audit.
Release the handles and step away.

speaker: Prism Controls
text: Pressure rises at the Lens. The safety latch restores the controls before containment can rupture. The relief needs a channel that carries flow away.

speaker: Prism Controls
text: The return closes and pressure stops draining. The safety latch resets all three handles. Keep the relief path open while isolating its supply.

speaker: Prism Controls
text: The audit continuity lamp turns amber. The safety latch resets the handles without sending an alarm. The gold circuit needs a local substitute for its reporting signal.

speaker: Museum Curator
text: Your registry entry is adequate. Keep the service corridors clear for the paying guests.

speaker: Hacked Lab Terminal
text: Calibration accepted. Operator telemetry awaits removal at the Landing Pad Roof test relay.

speaker: Mika
text: The lanterns have power. Use the market registry broadcast above the stalls so patrols stop listing us as abandoned.

speaker: Dock Interlock
text: Simulation ready. Cycling either outer seal will vent the dock for a second. The torn seam under the carpet is all that separates the worker passage from the dock. Which seal do you close first?

options.text: Seal the docking collar.
Isolate the red carpet seam.
Seal the observation glass.
Leave the controls.

speaker: Dock Interlock
text: Worker passage isolated. The glass seal needs pressure to seat. Its supply line is bleeding air at the docking collar. What closes next?

options.text: Seal the docking collar.
Seal the observation glass.
Start over.

speaker: Dock Interlock
text: Docking collar sealed. Pressure is back at the glass. One breach remains against open space.

options.text: Release the carpet bulkhead.
Seal the observation glass.

speaker: Dock Interlock
text: Simulation aborted. Keep the worker passage sealed while the dock is exposed. The glass seal can only seat once the collar holds pressure. The live bulkheads are still in place.

options.text: Reset the simulation.
Leave the controls.

speaker: Dock Interlock
text: Sequence verified. Applying all three seals. Dock pressure is stable. Access priority is a separate control; the workers are still locked out.

speaker: Dock Interlock
text: Simulation suspended. No pressure controls changed.

speaker: Nova
text: Nova. We came from the mining colony. We need somewhere to stop moving before those patrols find us.

speaker: Jax
text: Then get off the street. There's an empty apartment above the bar. The last tenants left when the sweeps started; I've kept the power on. You can catch your breath there. Keep the stairs clear and trouble away from my customers. That's the deal.

speaker: Museum Curator
text: [The Curator blocks the registry with one immaculate sleeve.] Maintenance, then? State your work order. I will not have contractors wandering through the orchids.

options.text: Scheduled air-filter inspection.
Emergency glass repair.
Private delivery for a guest.
Step away from the registry.

speaker: Museum Curator
text: [Zeke taps the folded service order in Nova's hand. The copied clearance authorizes scheduled work.] An emergency? There is no damage report. Incident number?

speaker: Museum Curator
text: [The Curator waits, enjoying this. The folded service order is still in Nova's hand.] Guest deliveries use the concierge. You are wearing maintenance uniforms.

speaker: Nova
text: [Nova checks the folded work order again.]

options.text: Correct the request: scheduled air-filter inspection.
Step away and review the service order.

speaker: Museum Curator
text: [The registry matches the work order to your copied badges. The Curator moves his sleeve.] Air filters. Of course. Try not to touch anything a guest might see.

speaker: Nova
text: [Nova sets the records on the table.] You said you stayed right here?

options.text: Your badge entered the Syndicate Booth at 21:14.
Your comms unit vented coolant at 21:12.
The dispenser poured a drink at 21:15.
Review the evidence before continuing.

speaker: Director Sorrell
text: A unit can vent while I sit beside it. Show me a record of me leaving the table.

speaker: Director Sorrell
text: Of course the dispenser logged it. Where does it say I went to the booth?

speaker: Nova
text: [Nova keeps a finger on the access log and pulls the other evidence closer.] All right. Look at the glass.

options.text: Coolant in the glass matches the missing core in your comms rig.
The badge timestamp repeats your name.
The dispenser poured the drink without additives.
Step back and compare the evidence.

speaker: Director Sorrell
